To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
syncytial germ cell cysts migrate across the blood testes barrier in adult mice by forming a network of compartments that are transiently bounded by tight junctions.
syncytial germ cells migrate across the blood testes barrier by traversing a series of compartments bounded by new and old tight junctions.

(1) the blood testis (BT) barrier is a syncytial network of compartments that is formed by old and new strands of tight junction (TJ) proteins, (2) germ cell cysts transit the BT barrier in syncytia that span the transient compartments, (3) transit occurs in a stepwise manner that involves dissolution of the old TJ network and formation of the new network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of tight junctions in the development of epithelia and in their maintenance in adult tissues.
the mechanisms that regulate the formation and maintenance of tight junctions in the seminiferous epithelium.
the mechanisms of germ cell migration across Sertoli cell junctions and the role of tight junction proteins in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
germ cell cysts are enclosed within transient compartments bounded by old tight junctions that are subsequently dissolved, allowing the germ cells to enter the adluminal space.
tight junctions are dynamic structures that are continuously being remodeled to allow germ cell cysts to transit across the blood–testis barrier.
the blood testis barriers are formed in a way that allows the transit of germ cell cysts across the barrier without compromising the integrity of the barrier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
germ cells migrate across the blood testes barrier in adult mice by traversing transient compartments that are bounded by new tight junctions, which are formed at the expense of old ones.
the Sertoli cells build compartments around the cysts to prevent damage to the SCTJs.
the blood-testis barrier is a dynamic structure, which is continuously remodeled during spermatogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
germ cells are released into the lumen of seminiferous epithelium in the adult testis.
Sertoli cells create a network of compartments that allows germ cells to transit the barrier.
the blood testis barriers in adult mice are dynamic structures that undergo periodic reassembly and remodeling.
